title: KV cache time-aware retention and cohorting spec
content:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a time-aware retention and cohorting approach for the KV cache aimed at reducing fragmentation, improving effective hit-rate across mixed LRU/MRU workloads, and bounding tail latency impact from large-object churn. It is intentionally orthogonal to existing slab/buddy designs and focuses on request-pattern-driven placement and reclamation.

Context and motivation:
- We observe two common patterns that drive inefficiency: (1) large transient prefixes that pollute the cache and cause churn for small hot entries, (2) long-tailed access distributions where entries oscillate between hot and cold across minutes. Traditional LRU or pure size-based eviction either evict long-lived small items too aggressively or keep large transient items too long, increasing fragmentation and OOM pressure.

Goals:
1) Reduce allocation fragmentation for heterogeneous item sizes.
2) Ensure small, high-value entries are shielded from large bursty allocations.
3) Provide predictable worst-case reclamation latency for background compaction.
4) Allow tunable tradeoff between hit-rate and memory utilization per shard.

High-level idea:
- Cohorts: partition cache entries into 3 logical cohorts based on recent access patterns and estimated lifetime: Transient (burst-only), Stable (frequently touched, long-lived), and Cooling (recently demoted). Cohorts are orthogonal to physical pools and are represented by metadata bits attached to entries.
- Time-aware retention score: each entry has a compact decay score computed from last-N-access timestamps (exponentially decayed). The score drives cohort assignment and eviction priority.
- Size-buckets + small-object shield: small entries (< 1 KB) are protected by a dedicated fast-path pool (small-pool) with its own quota and admission window to avoid being displaced by large allocations.

Memory pools and layout:
- Two-level layout: global slab arena for small objects (power-of-two size classes up to 4KB), and a general-purpose variable-slot arena for medium/large objects. The variable-slot arena uses an allocation header with a 64-bit tag that includes cohort, decay-score bucket, and a compact size tag.
- Per-shard quota: each cache shard has a soft quota for small-pool that can be borrowed from the global reserve on burst, with a fast reclaim path to enforce soft limits.
- Fragmentation mitigation: large-object allocations prefer segregated extents that are aligned to 64 KB boundaries to make coalescing easier. Background compaction coalesces free extents in epoch windows to avoid holding the allocator lock for long.

Admission and promotion rules:
- New entries start as Transient with a short probation window (configurable default: 15s). If reaccessed within the window, they are promoted to Stable. Reaccess pattern is evaluated using a bloom-window sketch per-shard to avoid per-entry counters.
- Cooling cohort is a lightweight FIFO list of demoted stable entries; entries demoted into Cooling get a grace-retention equal to half the shard's average inter-arrival time to reduce ping-pong.

Eviction policy (hybrid):
- Eviction selects victims by cohort priority first: Transient >> Cooling >> Stable. Within cohort, victims are chosen by a composite key: (decay-score, size-class, last-access timestamp) where decay-score has exponential weight to prefer evicting items whose recent accesses have decayed.
- Small-pool enforcement: when small-pool exceeds quota, a fast-path reclaim scans the small-pool hot list and evicts lowest-scored entries. This scan is bounded (max pages per reclaim) to bound tail latency.
- Large-object fallback: if insufficient space in variable-slot arena, allocator triggers an extent-split/partial-compact attempt. If that fails, we escalate eviction into Stable cohort with a stricter threshold.

Compaction and background work:
- Epochal compaction windows: compaction runs in background with work-limited epochs (e.g., max 20ms per shard per minute) to coalesce free extents and defragment the variable-slot arena.
- Live-copy vs tombstone: default is in-place free with tombstone bitmap for quick reuse; compaction performs live-copy of still-referenced objects during low-traffic windows only.
- Garbage estimation: use sampling of allocation headers to estimate fragmentation ratio and trigger more aggressive compaction when the estimated external fragmentation crosses a threshold.

Observability and metrics:
- Per-shard: cohort counts, small-pool usage, avg decay-score by cohort, fragmentation ratio estimate, compaction time per epoch, eviction counts by cohort and size-class.
- Alerts: sustained growth in Transient cohort (possible burst leak), fragmentation ratio > 0.3 for > 5m, compaction backlog > 3 epochs.

Evaluation plan / experiments:
1) Replay production allocation traces into a simulator that implements cohorting and time-aware decay; compare hit-rate and fragmentation vs current LRU baseline.
2) Stress test with synthetic large transient prefixes to validate small-pool shield.
3) Measure worst-case concurrent reclaim latency with bounded-epoch compaction settings.

Rollout and configuration knobs:
- Feature gate: cohorting can be enabled per-deployment as an opt-in flag.
- Tunables: probation window, small-pool quota per shard, decay half-life, compaction epoch budget, cohort demotion grace. Sensible defaults provided for hosted vs dedicated (dedicated allowing more aggressive compaction).

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Bloom-window false positives: the bloom approach reduces per-entry counters but introduces false promotions; need to test sensitivity.
- Memory overhead: per-entry header currently ~8 bytes; need to evaluate at scale.
- Cold-start warmup: how to prime Stable cohort when serving a new model? Consider prewarming on model load using evaluation traces.

References and links:
- Prototype simulator: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tree/main/tools/kv-sim
- Design notes (related): JIRA-RT-987, internal chat thread #kv-alloc

Next steps:
- Build a trace-driven simulator and run against 72 hours of production traces (owner: Marco).
- PR for allocator metadata layout and API (owner: Aisha).
- Instrument per-shard metrics and dashboard before enabling feature gate in canary.
